text: Rohan, a mid-level manager in a rapidly growing organization, is known for taking independent decisions and handling challenging situations confidently. However, his approach varies across situations. At times, he strongly believes in his ability to influence outcomes and readily takes responsibility for the results of his decisions. In other situations, he becomes doubtful about his own capabilities and tends to attribute setbacks to circumstances beyond his control. His team has also observed that these perceptions influence the way he responds to criticism, evaluates alternatives, and makes managerial decisions. Analyse the scenario and identify the underlying personality-related factors influencing Rohan's behaviour and decision-making. Explain how these factors may account for the differences in his responses across situations.
note: Personality factors such as locus of control and self-efficacy are not in the OML decks yet.

text: A global organization has introduced a common work policy across its international offices. While some employees appreciate the policy, others report concerns about long working hours, family commitments, leave practices, and expectations of availability after work. Managers also observe that these concerns vary across countries due to differences in local regulations and cultural expectations. Based on the scenario, critically evaluate how the political and cultural environment may influence work-life balance and behaviour of an individual in a multicultural organization. Suggest suitable measures to address these differences.
note: The slides list globalization, diversity and managing in the global village as OB challenges, but work-life balance and the political and cultural environment of the individual are not taught.
